patches.concept: combine masses; one percentage loss; divide by a known number of packets
patches.scenario: one-stage loss after total mass addition

replacement.stem: A factory starts with $6\times10^{9}$ g of material and receives another $2\times10^{8}$ g. After $10\%$ of the combined mass is lost, the rest is packed equally into $5\times10^{7}$ packets. Find the mass in grams of one packet, in standard form.

options.misconception: Add 10% rather than remove it: 1.1×6.2×10^9 / 5×10^7 =136.4 g.
Forget the received material, then remove 10%: 0.9×6×10^9 / 5×10^7 =108 g.
Keep the removed 10% instead of the remaining 90%: 0.1×6.2×10^9 / 5×10^7 =12.4 g.

patches.concept: percentage loss followed by fixed absolute reserve; order of operations

replacement.stem: A factory begins with $7\times10^{9}$ g of powder. It loses $15\%$ during processing, then sets aside $2\times10^{8}$ g of the remaining powder for testing. The rest is divided equally between $4\times10^{7}$ bags. Calculate the mass of powder in one bag in grams, in standard form.

options.misconception: Ignore the separately reserved 2×10^8 g: (0.85×7×10^9)/(4×10^7)=148.75 g.
Apply the 15% processing loss twice before reserving: (0.85²×7×10^9−2×10^8)/(4×10^7)=121.4375 g.
Add the testing reserve rather than subtract: (0.85×7×10^9+2×10^8)/(4×10^7)=153.75 g.
Reserve the 2×10^8 g first, then apply loss to everything left: 0.85×(7×10^9−2×10^8)/(4×10^7)=144.5 g.
Retain 15% instead of 85%, then reserve the fixed amount: (0.15×7×10^9−2×10^8)/(4×10^7)=21.25 g.

workedSolutionSteps: Set aside $2\times10^8$ g: packable mass $=5.75\times10^9$ g.
Divide by $4\times10^7$: one bag contains $1.4375\times10^2$ g.

patches.concept: reverse percentage to recover original quantity from final number and mass per packet

replacement.stem: A factory loses $20\%$ of its starting mass in processing, then adds $1.2\times10^{8}$ g of a second material. It fills $4\times10^{6}$ packets, each containing $2.1\times10^{2}$ g. Find the starting mass before the loss, in grams, in standard form.

options.misconception: Subtract added mass but forget to reverse the loss: 4×10^6×210−1.2×10^8=7.2×10^8 g.
Treat retained 7.2×10^8 g as 20% (lost portion) rather than 80%: 7.2×10^8/0.2=3.6×10^9 g.
Add the second material again when reversing the loss instead of subtracting: (8.4×10^8+1.2×10^8)/0.8=1.2×10^9 g.
Apply a further 20% loss rather than reverse it: 7.2×10^8×0.8=5.76×10^8 g.
Forget to subtract the added material before reversing: 8.4×10^8/0.8=1.05×10^9 g.

workedSolutionSteps: Mass after the 20% loss but before addition $=8.4\times10^8-1.2\times10^8=7.2\times10^8$ g.
This is 80% of starting mass: $7.2\times10^8/0.8=9\times10^8$ g.

patches.concept: successive percentage losses on successive remaining quantities

replacement.stem: A factory processes $4.5\times10^{9}$ g of a product. First it loses $20\%$ of the mass. During inspection, a further $25\%$ of the mass then remaining is rejected. The accepted mass is divided equally into $3\times10^{7}$ packets. Find the mass in grams of one packet, in standard form.

options.misconception: Ignore the second 25% loss: 4.5×10^9×0.8/(3×10^7)=120 g.
Keep only 20% in the first stage instead of 80%: 4.5×10^9×0.2×0.75/(3×10^7)=22.5 g.
Add 25% instead of losing 25% at inspection: 4.5×10^9×0.8×1.25/(3×10^7)=150 g.

workedSolutionSteps: After the first loss, $0.8(4.5\times10^9)=3.6\times10^9$ g remains.
After the second loss, retain 75% of this: $0.75(3.6\times10^9)=2.7\times10^9$ g.
Dividing by $3\times10^7$ packets gives $9\times10^1$ g each.
